title: Legal & Contracts II
completion_message: ¡Formidable! El vocabulario legal de nivel C2 es el escudo protector de cualquier corporación. Conceptos como 'Indemnity', 'Force Majeure' y 'Breach of contract' aseguran que tus negociaciones sean impecables y legalmente blindadas.

parts.visual:
1. Indemnity / To indemnify (Indemnización / Eximir de responsabilidad): 
- Protección o compensación financiera contra una pérdida, daño o responsabilidad. 
Ej: The contract includes an INDEMNITY clause protecting us from third-party lawsuits. 
Ej: You must INDEMNIFY the company against any losses. 

2. Liability / Liable (Responsabilidad legal / Responsable legalmente): 
- Ser legalmente responsable de algo (una deuda o daño). 
Ej: The company accepted full LIABILITY for the accident. 
Ej: If the product fails, the manufacturer is LIABLE.
parts.audio: Welcome to Advanced Legal English. Number 1: Indemnity and the verb To indemnify. This means protection or financial compensation against a loss, damage, or legal liability. For example: The contract includes an INDEMNITY clause protecting us from third-party lawsuits. Or: You must INDEMNIFY the company against any losses. Number 2: Liability, and the adjective Liable. This means being legally responsible for something, like a debt or damage. For example: The company accepted full LIABILITY for the accident. Or: If the product fails, the manufacturer is LIABLE.

parts.visual:
3. Breach of contract (Incumplimiento de contrato): 
- Fallar en cumplir los términos de un acuerdo legal. 
Ej: Failing to deliver the goods on time constitutes a BREACH OF CONTRACT. 

4. Force Majeure (Fuerza mayor / Act of God): 
- Un evento imprevisible o inevitable (desastre natural, guerra) que exime a las partes de cumplir el contrato. 
Ej: The shipment was delayed due to a hurricane, invoking the FORCE MAJEURE clause. 

5. Null and void (Nulo y sin valor): 
- Sin validez legal. 
Ej: If you alter this document, the agreement becomes NULL AND VOID.
parts.audio: Number 3: Breach of contract. This means failing to fulfill the terms of a legal agreement. For example: Failing to deliver the goods on time constitutes a BREACH OF CONTRACT. Number 4: Force Majeure, also known as an Act of God. An unforeseeable or unavoidable event, like a natural disaster or war, that excuses parties from fulfilling the contract. For example: The shipment was delayed due to a hurricane, invoking the FORCE MAJEURE clause. Number 5: Null and void. This means having no legal validity. For example: If you alter this document, the agreement becomes NULL AND VOID.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término legal corporativo correcto.

questions.question: The contractor must ____ the company against any claims made by third parties. (Indemnizar / Eximir de responsabilidad).
Because of the accident on their property, the corporation faces massive legal ____. (Responsabilidad legal).
Refusing to pay the agreed amount is a clear ____ of contract. (Incumplimiento).
questions.explanation: Breach of contract = incumplimiento de contrato.

questions.question: Due to the earthquake, the company invoked the ____ Majeure clause to cancel the shipments. (Fuerza mayor).
questions.explanation: Force Majeure (o Act of God) = Fuerza mayor.

questions.question: Because it was signed by a minor, the judge declared the contract null and ____. (Nulo y sin valor).
questions.explanation: Null and void = nulo y sin valor legal.

questions.question: The law firm drafted a non-____ agreement (NDA) to protect the trade secrets.
If you drive drunk, you are personally ____ for any damages you cause. (Responsable legalmente).
Before signing, the lawyers must conduct thorough due ____ to investigate the company's finances. (Diligencia debida).
questions.explanation: Due diligence = auditoría/diligencia debida antes de una compra/contrato.

questions.question: The contract includes a ____ clause, allowing either party to end the agreement with 30 days' notice. (Terminación).
Any disputes will be settled by ____ rather than going to a public court. (Arbitraje).
The new legislation will come into ____ on January 1st. (Entrar en vigor).
questions.explanation: Come into effect (o enter into force) = entrar en vigor.

questions.question: The developer claims full intellectual ____ rights over the software code.
A formal, written promise to do something or pay money is a ____. (Pacto/Convenio legal).
If you fail to pay the mortgage, the bank can ____ the property. (Embargar/Ejecutar hipoteca).
The employee signed a non-____ clause, meaning she cannot work for a rival company for two years.
questions.explanation: Non-compete clause = cláusula de no competencia.

questions.question: He was accused of ____ of duty for failing to protect the company's assets. (Incumplimiento de deber).
questions.explanation: Breach of duty = incumplimiento del deber.

questions.question: We demand financial ____ for the damages caused by your negligence. (Compensación económica/indemnización).
The ____ text of the law is very ambiguous and open to interpretation. (Estatutario / Legal).
questions.explanation: Statutory = establecido por estatuto o ley.

questions.question: Both parties must act in good ____ during the negotiation process. (Buena fe).
A legal decision that serves as a rule or pattern in future similar cases is a ____. (Precedente).
questions.explanation: Set a precedent = sentar un precedente.

questions.question: To ____ the company. (Proteger/Indemnizar con I)
Legal ____. (Responsabilidad con L)
He is legally ____. (Responsable adjetivo con L)
____ of contract. (Incumplimiento con B)
Force ____. (Fuerza mayor con M)
Null and ____. (Sin valor legal con V)
Due ____. (Diligencia debida/Auditoría previa con D)
Go to ____. (Arbitraje con A)
Intellectual ____. (Propiedad con P)
In good ____. (Buena fe con F)
